# Excel Lab
## One-Sample, Independent-Samples, and Paired t-tests with the Iris Dataset

---

# Lab Overview and Dataset Features

.pull-left[
## Overview
- In this lab, you will use Excel to run all **three t-test designs** we covered in lecture, using the familiar Iris dataset:
  - a **one-sample** t-test
  - an **independent-samples** t-test
  - a **paired-samples** t-test
- No new data to download and re-learn &mdash; same Iris dataset, new questions.
]

--
.pull-right[
## Key Features:
- 150 observations of iris flowers.
- Four numeric features:
  - Sepal.Length
  - Sepal.Width
  - Petal.Length
  - Petal.Width
- Three species:
  - Setosa
  - Versicolor
  - Virginica
]


---

class: middle, inverse

# Task 1
## One-Sample t-test: Is Sepal Length 5 cm?

---

# Task 1: Overview
.pull-left[
In this task, we will:
- Test whether the **mean Sepal.Length** of our 150 flowers differs from a hypothesized value, $\mu_0 = 5$ cm.
- Compute the test **manually**, step by step, using `AVERAGE`, `STDEV.S`, and the t-formula.
- Use `T.DIST.2T` / `T.INV.2T` to get the critical value and p-value.
]
.pull-right[
```{r, echo=FALSE, out.width="90%", warning = FALSE}
knitr::include_graphics("../img/DALLE_exceldoodle.png")
```
]
---

## Step 0: Download the Iris Dataset

.pull-left-wide[
```{r, echo=TRUE}
iris_onesample <- iris %>% select(Sepal.Length)

# Save the dataset as an Excel file
write.xlsx(iris_onesample, "IrisData_OneSample.xlsx")
```

[Download the Excel file here](https://github.com/psychmethods/slides/raw/refs/heads/main/t12_t-test/IrisData_OneSample.xlsx)
]
.pull-right-narrow[
.center[
```{r, echo=FALSE, out.width="100%", warning = FALSE}
library(qrcode)

share_link <- "https://github.com/psychmethods/slides/raw/refs/heads/main/t12_t-test/IrisData_OneSample.xlsx"
code <- qr_code(share_link)

plot(code)
```
]]

.footnote[or here https://github.com/psychmethods/slides/raw/refs/heads/main/t12_t-test/IrisData_OneSample.xlsx]

---

# Step 1: Calculate the Mean and SD

.pull-left[
1. Open the Excel file `IrisData_OneSample.xlsx`.

2. **Select a cell** for the mean (e.g., B152) and enter:
   - `=AVERAGE(A2:A151)`

3. **Select another cell** for the standard deviation (e.g., B153) and enter:
   - `=STDEV.S(A2:A151)`

4. Press Enter after each formula to see the result.
]
--
.pull-right[
```{r, echo=FALSE, out.width="90%", fig.align='center'}
image_path <- "../img/excel_lab/excel screenshot_1.png"
img <- image_read(image_path) %>%
  image_annotate("=AVERAGE(A2:A151)", size = 30, color = "red", location = "+550+475")
img
```

**Explanation**:
- Unlike the Z-score lab, we don't know the **population** mean or SD &mdash; only the sample's. That's exactly why we need a **t-test** instead of a Z-test.
]
---

# Step 2: Set Up the Hypotheses

```{r}
onesample_test <- t.test(iris$Sepal.Length, mu = 5)
os_mean <- round(mean(iris$Sepal.Length), 2)
os_sd   <- round(sd(iris$Sepal.Length), 2)
os_n    <- nrow(iris)
os_t    <- round(onesample_test$statistic, 2)
os_df   <- unname(onesample_test$parameter)
os_p    <- format.pval(onesample_test$p.value, digits = 3, eps = .001)
os_crit <- round(qt(0.975, os_df), 3)
```

.pull-left[
- Null hypothesis, $H_0$: $\mu = 5$ cm
- Alternative hypothesis, $H_1$: $\mu \ne 5$ cm
- Tails: two-tailed
]
.pull-right[
- What we have:
  - $\bar{x} =$ `r os_mean`
  - $s =$ `r os_sd`
  - $n =$ `r os_n`
  - $\mu_0 = 5$
]

---

# Step 3: Compute the t-statistic

.pull-left[
1. **Select a new cell** (e.g., B154) for the standard error:
   - `=B153/SQRT(COUNT(A2:A151))`

2. **Select another cell** (e.g., B155) for the t-statistic:
   - `=(B152-5)/B154`

   This is just:
   $$t = \frac{\bar{x}-\mu_0}{s/\sqrt{n}} = \frac{\text{`r os_mean`} - 5}{\text{`r os_sd`}/\sqrt{\text{`r os_n`}}} = \text{`r os_t`}$$
]
--
.pull-right[
```{r, echo=FALSE, out.width="90%", fig.align='center'}
image_path <- "../img/excel_lab/excel screenshot_zoom.png"
img <- image_read(image_path) %>%
  image_annotate("=(B152-5)/B154", size = 30, color = "blue", location = "+550+475")
img
```
]

---

# Step 4: Find the Critical Value and p-value

.pull-left[
1. **Degrees of freedom** (e.g., B156): `=COUNT(A2:A151)-1` &rarr; df = `r os_df`

2. **Critical value** (two-tailed, $\alpha=.05$), in a new cell:
   - `=T.INV.2T(0.05, B156)`
   - t\* = `r os_crit`

3. **Exact p-value**, in a new cell:
   - `=T.DIST.2T(ABS(B155), B156)`
   - p `r ifelse(onesample_test$p.value < .001, "< .001", paste0("= ", os_p))`
]
--
.pull-right[
```{r, echo=FALSE, out.width="90%", fig.align='center'}
image_path <- "../img/excel_lab/excel screenshot_1.png"
img <- image_read(image_path) %>%
  image_annotate("=T.DIST.2T(ABS(t), df)", size = 28, color = "darkgreen", location = "+500+475")
img
```

**Explanation**:
- `T.DIST.2T()` returns the two-tailed p-value for a t-statistic. `T.INV.2T()` works in reverse: give it a probability, it gives you the critical t-value.
]

---

# Step 5: Make a Decision

- $t$ = `r os_t`, df = `r os_df`, p `r if (onesample_test$p.value < .001) "< .001" else paste0("= ", os_p)`
- Compare $|t|$ = `r abs(os_t)` to $t^*$ = `r os_crit`: `r ifelse(abs(os_t) > os_crit, "reject", "fail to reject")` $H_0$.
- The 95% CI for the mean Sepal.Length is [`r round(onesample_test$conf.int[1],2)`, `r round(onesample_test$conf.int[2],2)`], which `r ifelse(onesample_test$conf.int[1] <= 5 & onesample_test$conf.int[2] >= 5, "includes", "does not include")` 5.

.reminder[Try re-running this with a different hypothesized mean (e.g., $\mu_0=5.8$) and see how the decision changes.]

---

# Task 1 Recap: One-Sample t-test

In this section, you:
- Calculated the **mean** and **standard deviation** of `Sepal.Length`.
- Computed a **t-statistic by hand**, using the sample SE in place of the (unknown) population SD.
- Used `T.INV.2T()` and `T.DIST.2T()` to find the critical value and p-value.
- Decided whether to reject $H_0: \mu = 5$.

---

class: center, middle, inverse

# Task 2
## Independent-Samples t-test: Versicolor vs. Virginica

---

# Task 2: Overview

.pull-left[
- **Visualize** `Petal.Length` for two species with a boxplot.
- **Test** whether the mean `Petal.Length` differs between *versicolor* and *virginica* using Excel's `T.TEST()` function.
- Compare the **pooled-variance** and **Welch-corrected** versions of the test.
]
.pull-right[
```{r, echo=FALSE, out.width="80%", warning = FALSE}
knitr::include_graphics("../img/DALLE_Fisher_looking_at_flowers.png")
```
]

---

## Step 0: Download the Two-Species Dataset

.pull-left[

We'll compare two columns, one per species:
- **Versicolor** `Petal.Length`
- **Virginica** `Petal.Length`

```{r, echo=TRUE}
versicolor <- iris %>% filter(Species == "versicolor") %>% pull(Petal.Length)
virginica  <- iris %>% filter(Species == "virginica")  %>% pull(Petal.Length)

iris_twogroups <- data.frame(Versicolor = versicolor, Virginica = virginica)

# Save the dataset as an Excel file
write.xlsx(iris_twogroups, "IrisData_Independent.xlsx")
```

[Download the Excel file here](https://github.com/psychmethods/slides/raw/refs/heads/main/t12_t-test/IrisData_Independent.xlsx)
```{r, echo=FALSE, out.width="40%", warning = FALSE}
library(qrcode)

share_link <- "https://github.com/psychmethods/slides/raw/refs/heads/main/t12_t-test/IrisData_Independent.xlsx"
code <- qr_code(share_link)

plot(code)
```

]

.pull-right[
.center[
```{r, echo=FALSE, out.width="90%", fig.align='center', warning=FALSE}
ggplot(iris %>% filter(Species %in% c("versicolor", "virginica")),
       aes(x = Species, y = Petal.Length, fill = Species)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "none") +
  labs(title = "Petal Length by Species", y = "Petal Length (cm)")
```
]]

.footnote[Both groups have 50 flowers, so they line up neatly in two columns.]

---

# Step 1: Calculate Group Means and SDs

.pull-left[
1. **Select cells** below each column (e.g., B52 and C52) and enter:
   - `=AVERAGE(A2:A51)` for Versicolor
   - `=AVERAGE(B2:B51)` for Virginica

2. **Below those** (e.g., B53, C53), enter:
   - `=STDEV.S(A2:A51)`
   - `=STDEV.S(B2:B51)`
]
--
.pull-right[
```{r, echo=FALSE, out.width="90%", fig.align='center'}
image_path <- "../img/excel_lab/excel screenshot_zoom.png"
img <- image_read(image_path) %>%
  image_annotate("=AVERAGE(A2:A51)", size = 30, color = "darkgreen", location = "+550+475")
img
```

```{r}
ind_mean_vc <- round(mean(versicolor), 2)
ind_sd_vc   <- round(sd(versicolor), 2)
ind_mean_vg <- round(mean(virginica), 2)
ind_sd_vg   <- round(sd(virginica), 2)
```

Versicolor: $\bar{x}=$ `r ind_mean_vc`, $s=$ `r ind_sd_vc`
<br>
Virginica: $\bar{x}=$ `r ind_mean_vg`, $s=$ `r ind_sd_vg`
]

---

# Step 2: Run `T.TEST()`

.pull-left[
1. **Select an empty cell** and enter:
   - `=T.TEST(A2:A51, B2:B51, 2, 3)`

2. The arguments are: `array1, array2, tails, type`
   - `tails = 2` &rarr; two-tailed test
   - `type = 3` &rarr; **Welch's correction** (unequal variances)
   - `type = 2` would assume **equal variances** (pooled)

3. The result is the **p-value directly** &mdash; no critical-value lookup needed!
]
--
.pull-right[
```{r, echo=FALSE, out.width="90%", fig.align='center'}
image_path <- "../img/excel_lab/excel screenshot_1.png"
img <- image_read(image_path) %>%
  image_annotate("=T.TEST(A2:A51,B2:B51,2,3)", size = 24, color = "purple", location = "+480+475")
img
```

```{r}
welch_test  <- t.test(virginica, versicolor)
pooled_test <- t.test(virginica, versicolor, var.equal = TRUE)
ind_t   <- round(welch_test$statistic, 2)
ind_df  <- round(unname(welch_test$parameter), 2)
ind_p   <- format.pval(welch_test$p.value, digits = 3, eps = .001)
```

Welch: t = `r ind_t`, df = `r ind_df`, p `r ifelse(welch_test$p.value < .001, "< .001", paste0("= ", ind_p))`
]

---

# Step 3: Equal Variance or Not?

.pull-left-narrow[
- `T.TEST()`'s `type` argument matters:
  - `type = 2`: pooled/equal-variance t-test
  - `type = 3`: Welch's t-test (unequal variance)
- Check variances first with `=VAR.S()` on each column, or just eyeball the boxplot spread from Step 0.
]
.pull-right-wide[
```{r}
pooled_p <- format.pval(pooled_test$p.value, digits = 3, eps = .001)
```
- Pooled (type = 2): p `r ifelse(pooled_test$p.value < .001, "< .001", paste0("= ", pooled_p))`
- Welch (type = 3): p `r ifelse(welch_test$p.value < .001, "< .001", paste0("= ", ind_p))`
- Here the two barely differ &mdash; but when group sizes or spreads are very different, the choice of `type` can change your conclusion.
]

---

# Step 4: Make a Decision

- Mean difference (Virginica $-$ Versicolor) = `r round(ind_mean_vg - ind_mean_vc, 2)` cm, 95% CI [`r round(welch_test$conf.int[1],2)`, `r round(welch_test$conf.int[2],2)`]
- t = `r ind_t`, df = `r ind_df`, p `r ifelse(welch_test$p.value < .001, "< .001", paste0("= ", ind_p))`
- `r ifelse(welch_test$p.value < .05, "Reject", "Do not reject")` $H_0$: there `r ifelse(welch_test$p.value < .05, "is", "is not")` evidence that mean Petal.Length differs between the two species.

---

# Task 2 Recap: Independent-Samples t-test

- In this section, you:
  - Visualized `Petal.Length` by species with a **boxplot**.
  - Used Excel's **`T.TEST()`** function to compare two independent groups directly &mdash; no manual t-formula needed.
  - Compared the **pooled** (`type = 2`) and **Welch** (`type = 3`) versions of the test.

.reminder[Be sure to save your Excel file with the boxplot and T.TEST results for future reference.]

---

class: middle, inverse

# Task 3
## Paired-Samples t-test: Sepal vs. Petal Length

---

# Task 3: Overview

- In this task, we will:
  - Treat `Sepal.Length` and `Petal.Length` as a **matched pair** &mdash; two measurements taken on the *same* flower.
  - **Compute difference scores** and test whether their mean differs from zero.
  - Confirm the manual result with Excel's `T.TEST()` paired shortcut.

---

# Step 0: Download the Paired Dataset

.pull-left[
- Each row is **one flower**, with both measurements side by side &mdash; that's what makes this a *paired* design.

```{r, echo=TRUE}
iris_paired <- iris %>% select(Sepal.Length, Petal.Length)

# Save the dataset as an Excel file
write.xlsx(iris_paired, "IrisData_Paired.xlsx")
```

[Download the Excel file here](https://github.com/psychmethods/slides/raw/refs/heads/main/t12_t-test/IrisData_Paired.xlsx)
]

.pull-right[
.center[
```{r, echo=FALSE, out.width="60%", warning = FALSE}
library(qrcode)

share_link <- "https://github.com/psychmethods/slides/raw/refs/heads/main/t12_t-test/IrisData_Paired.xlsx"
code <- qr_code(share_link)

plot(code)
```
]]

.footnote[Sepal.Length (A) and Petal.Length (B), same 150 flowers in both columns.]

---

# Step 1: Calculate the Difference Scores

.pull-left[
1. **Select cell C2** and enter:
   - `=A2-B2`

2. **Fill down**: drag the fill handle from C2 to C151 to compute the difference for every flower.

3. This gives you one difference score per flower: $d_i = \text{Sepal}_i - \text{Petal}_i$
]
--
.pull-right[
```{r, echo=FALSE, out.width="90%", fig.align='center'}
image_path <- "../img/excel_lab/excel screenshot_1.png"
img <- image_read(image_path) %>%
  image_annotate(" =A2-B2", size = 30, color = "darkgreen", location = "+550+475")
img
```
]

---

# Step 2: Mean and SD of the Differences

.pull-left[
1. **Select a cell** (e.g., C152) for the mean difference:
   - `=AVERAGE(C2:C151)`

2. **Select another cell** (e.g., C153) for the SD of the differences:
   - `=STDEV.S(C2:C151)`
]
--
.pull-right[
```{r, echo=FALSE, out.width="90%", fig.align='center'}
image_path <- "../img/excel_lab/excel screenshot_zoom.png"
img <- image_read(image_path) %>%
  image_annotate("=AVERAGE(C2:C151)", size = 30, color = "blue", location = "+550+475")
img
```

```{r}
paired_test <- t.test(iris$Sepal.Length, iris$Petal.Length, paired = TRUE)
pr_meandiff <- round(mean(iris$Sepal.Length - iris$Petal.Length), 2)
pr_sddiff   <- round(sd(iris$Sepal.Length - iris$Petal.Length), 2)
```

$\bar{d}=$ `r pr_meandiff`, $s_d=$ `r pr_sddiff`
]

---

# Step 3: Compute the t-statistic by Hand

.pull-left[
- Same formula as the one-sample test, applied to the **difference scores**:

$$t = \frac{\bar{d}}{s_d/\sqrt{n}} = \frac{\text{`r pr_meandiff`}}{\text{`r pr_sddiff`}/\sqrt{150}} = \text{`r round(paired_test$statistic,2)`}$$

- In Excel: `=C152/(C153/SQRT(150))`
]
--
.pull-right[
```{r, echo=FALSE, out.width="90%", fig.align='center'}
image_path <- "../img/excel_lab/excel screenshot_1.png"
img <- image_read(image_path) %>%
  image_annotate("=C152/(C153/SQRT(150))", size = 26, color = "red", location = "+480+475")
img
```
]

---

# Step 4: Check with `T.TEST()`

.pull-left[
1. **Select an empty cell** and enter:
   - `=T.TEST(A2:A151, B2:B151, 2, 1)`

2. `type = 1` tells Excel the two columns are **paired** (same `tails = 2` as before).

3. Compare this p-value to the one you'd get from your hand-calculated t-statistic &mdash; they should match!
]
--
.pull-right[
```{r, echo=FALSE, out.width="90%", fig.align='center'}
image_path <- "../img/excel_lab/excel screenshot_zoom.png"
img <- image_read(image_path) %>%
  image_annotate("=T.TEST(A2:A151,B2:B151,2,1)", size = 22, color = "purple", location = "+450+475")
img
```

```{r}
pr_p <- format.pval(paired_test$p.value, digits = 3, eps = .001)
```

p `r ifelse(paired_test$p.value < .001, "< .001", paste0("= ", pr_p))`
]

---

# Step 5: Make a Decision

- t = `r round(paired_test$statistic,2)`, df = `r unname(paired_test$parameter)`, p `r ifelse(paired_test$p.value < .001, "< .001", paste0("= ", pr_p))`
- Mean difference (Sepal $-$ Petal) = `r pr_meandiff` cm, 95% CI [`r round(paired_test$conf.int[1],2)`, `r round(paired_test$conf.int[2],2)`]
- `r ifelse(paired_test$p.value < .05, "Reject", "Do not reject")` $H_0: \mu_\Delta = 0$ &mdash; there `r ifelse(paired_test$p.value < .05, "is", "is not")` evidence that Sepal.Length and Petal.Length differ, on average, within the same flower.

---

# Task 3 Recap: Paired-Samples t-test

- In this section, you:
  - Recognized that two measurements on the *same* flower form a **paired** design.
  - Computed **difference scores** and ran a one-sample-style t-test on them.
  - Confirmed the manual result using Excel's **`T.TEST()`** paired shortcut (`type = 1`).

.reminder[Save your Excel file with the difference column and T.TEST results for future reference.]


---

class: center, middle, inverse

# Recap of Recaps

- In this lab, you ran all three t-test designs in Excel, using the Iris dataset throughout:
  - **One-sample** t-test (manual formula + `T.INV.2T`/`T.DIST.2T`)
  - **Independent-samples** t-test (`T.TEST()` with pooled vs. Welch correction)
  - **Paired-samples** t-test (difference scores + `T.TEST()` paired shortcut)
- In every case: same logic, same shape of formula &mdash; only what counts as "the sample" changes.
